#!/bin/bash
# usage: dt.sh [-v] case.txtar...   compare original vs mine
# A case is a txtar; the "-- @cmd --" section lists shell commands run from the
# case root, with $X standing for the executable under test.
MINE=${MINE:-/tmp/mybin}
ORIG=/workspace/executable
verbose=0
if [ "$1" = "-v" ]; then verbose=1; shift; fi
pass=0; fail=0
for c in "$@"; do
  name=$(basename "$c" .txtar)
  root=/tmp/dt/$name
  cmds=$(awk '/^-- @cmd --$/{f=1;next} /^-- .* --$/{f=0} f' "$c")
  files=$(awk '/^-- @cmd --$/{f=1;next} /^-- .* --$/{f=0} !f' "$c")
  i=0
  while IFS= read -r cmd; do
    [ -z "$cmd" ] && continue
    i=$((i+1))
    for which in orig mine; do
      echo "$files" | /tmp/mk.sh $root
      [ $which = orig ] && X=$ORIG || X=$MINE
      (cd $root && X=$X eval "$cmd" >/tmp/dt_$which.out 2>/tmp/dt_$which.err; echo $? >/tmp/dt_$which.code)
      (cd $root && find . -type f ! -path './.git/*' | sort | xargs -d '\n' sha1sum) > /tmp/dt_$which.files 2>/dev/null
      cp -r $root /tmp/dt_$which.tree.$$ 2>/dev/null; rm -rf /tmp/dt_${which}_tree; mv /tmp/dt_$which.tree.$$ /tmp/dt_${which}_tree
    done
    ok=1
    for k in out err code files; do
      if ! cmp -s /tmp/dt_orig.$k /tmp/dt_mine.$k; then ok=0; fi
    done
    if [ $ok = 1 ]; then pass=$((pass+1)); [ $verbose = 1 ] && echo "PASS $name #$i: $cmd"
    else fail=$((fail+1)); echo "FAIL $name #$i: $cmd"
      for k in out err code files; do
        if ! cmp -s /tmp/dt_orig.$k /tmp/dt_mine.$k; then echo "  --- $k differs:"; diff /tmp/dt_orig.$k /tmp/dt_mine.$k | head -${DIFFLINES:-20}; fi
      done
      if ! cmp -s /tmp/dt_orig.files /tmp/dt_mine.files; then diff -r /tmp/dt_orig_tree /tmp/dt_mine_tree | head -20; fi
    fi
  done <<< "$cmds"
done
echo "passed $pass, failed $fail"

Run them in the same order in CI. `shrink` exits 3 when it reports anything, as the analyzer does. With `-fix`, only the reports left without a fix count. ### Patterns The patterns only choose which packages are reported. To find uses, `shrink` always reads every package of the module, whatever the patterns name. For example, this reports only on `internal/user`: ```console $ declscope shrink ./internal/user/... internal/user/user.go:8:6: func Format is exported, but nothing outside example.com/app/internal/user uses it ``` `Load` is not reported, although `api/` is outside the pattern. `api/api.go` calls `user.Load`, and that call is a use. Otherwise, a pattern behaves as it does for `go vet`.
What counts as a use, and when the fix is withheld A fix is offered only where no use can exist outside the package. Where a use may exist but cannot be proved, the report stays and says why no fix is offered. results.content:
The `unused` rule reports a directive that changes nothing. A directive that declscope cannot read belongs to the [`directive`](#malformed-directives) rule instead.

#### Off, loose and strict

| `rules.unused` | `//declscope:ignore` is reported when | `//declscope:shared` or `//declscope:private` is reported when | `-fix` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `off` | Never | Never | None |
| `loose` | It silenced no report | Deleting it would change no declaration's scope under any config | None |
| `strict` *(default)* | It silenced no report | Deleting it would change no declaration's scope under the current config | Deletes a redundant scope directive, unless [withheld](#the-strict-fix) |

- One comment gets one report, however many declarations it reaches. A block's directive is reported once.
- Without the directive, a declaration falls to the next row of [scope resolution](#scope-resolution). Only `defaults.unexported` there depends on the config.
- Under `strict`, a directive that `loose` keeps also stays when deleting it would make a nearer directive redundant.
- `off` still leaves the `directive` rule on.
- An ignore of `boundary` is not reported where a file the build leaves out names a declaration it reaches, or for a field, its type: a literal written by position names only the type. That file may cross into it under another build tag, where the ignore silences the crossing. The run that reads the file still reports an ignore with nothing to silence.

> [!WARNING]
> Under `strict`, changing `defaults.unexported` changes the reports. With `unexported: shared`, every `//declscope:shared` on an unexported declaration that nothing else widens is reported, and one `-fix` run deletes them. `loose` never reports a directive only because it names the current default.

<details>
<summary>Example: one file under each mode</summary>

```go
package app

type user struct {
	//declscope:private
	name string
}

//declscope:shared
func Helper() {}

//declscope:ignore boundary
func greet(u user) string { return u.name }
```

| Line | `off` | `loose` | `strict` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 4 | Nothing | Nothing | `unused //declscope:private on user.name: it already has private scope` |
| 8 | Nothing | `unused //declscope:shared on Helper: nothing it reaches takes a scope` | `unused //declscope:shared on Helper: it already has shared scope` |
| 11 | Nothing | `unused //declscope:ignore boundary on greet` | `unused //declscope:ignore boundary on greet` |

Line 4 is where the modes differ. Deleting line 4 leaves `user.name` private only because `defaults.unexported` is private, which `loose` does not rely on.

</details>

#### Report messages

Every unused report names the directive and says why it is unused. `loose` and `strict` word the reason differently.

- Without the directive, a declaration falls to the next row of [scope resolution](#scope-resolution). Only `defaults.unexported` there depends on the config.
- Under `strict`, a directive that `loose` keeps also stays when deleting it would make a nearer directive redundant.
- `off` still leaves the `directive` rule on.

<details>
<summary>Example: one file under each mode</summary>

```go
package app

type user struct {
	//declscope:private
	name string
}

//declscope:shared
func Helper() {}

//declscope:ignore boundary
func greet(u user) string { return u.name }
```

| Line | `off` | `loose` | `strict` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 4 | Nothing | Nothing | `unused //declscope:private on user.name: it already has private scope` |
| 8 | Nothing | `unused //declscope:shared on Helper: nothing it reaches takes a scope` | `unused //declscope:shared on Helper: it already has shared scope` |
| 11 | Nothing | `unused //declscope:ignore boundary on greet` | `unused //declscope:ignore boundary on greet` |

Line 4 is where the modes differ. Deleting line 4 leaves `user.name` private only because `defaults.unexported` is private, which `loose` does not rely on.

</details>

Every unused report names the directive and says why it is unused. `loose` and `strict` word the reason differently.

import itertools
opts=["", "private", "shared"]
n=0
for F,B,S,exp,dflt,other,unused in itertools.product(opts,opts,opts,[False,True],["private","shared"],[False,True],["strict","loose"]):
    if not (F or B or S): continue
    name="A" if exp else "a"

    lines += ["package p",""]
    if B: lines.append("//declscope:"+B)

    lines.append("\t%s = 1" % name)
    lines.append(")")
    if other:
        lines += ["", "var other = 2"]
    use = "func useUser() { _ = %s%s }" % (name, "; _ = other" if other else "")
    n+=1
    with open("c%03d_%s_%s_%s_%s_%s_%s_%s.txtar"%(n,F or "-",B or "-",S or "-","E" if exp else "u",dflt,"o" if other else "n",unused),"w") as f:
        f.write("-- .declscope.yaml --\ndefaults:\n  unexported: %s\nrules:\n  unused: %s\n" % (dflt, unused))
        f.write("-- p/doc.go --\n" + "\n".join(lines) + "\n")
        f.write("-- p/user.go --\npackage p\n\n" + use + "\n")
        f.write("-- @cmd --\n$X -json ./...\n")
print(n)
EOF

# usage: combo_cmp.py case.txtar...   (runs both binaries on materialized case, prints unused diffs)
def run(binary, root):
    p = subprocess.run([binary, "-json", "./..."], cwd=root, capture_output=True, text=True)
    try:
        d = json.loads(p.stdout)
    except Exception:
        return ["ERR " + p.stderr.strip()]
    out = []
    for pkg, v in d.items():
        for an, diags in v.items():
            if isinstance(diags, dict):
                out.append("ERROR " + diags.get("error", ""))
                continue
            for x in diags:
                fx = x.get("suggested_fixes")
                pos = x["posn"].split("/")[-1]
                out.append("%s %s%s" % (pos, x["message"], "  [FIX]" if fx else ""))
    return out
for c in sys.argv[1:]:
    name = os.path.basename(c)[:-6]
    root = "/tmp/combo_root/" + name
    files = open(c).read().split("-- @cmd --")[0]
    subprocess.run(["/tmp/mk.sh", root], input=files, text=True)
    a = run("/workspace/executable", root)
    b = run("/tmp/mybin", root)
    if a != b:
        print("=== " + name)
        src = open(root + "/p/doc.go").read()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Random declscope scenario generator, richer Go: writes a txtar case to stdout."""
import random
import sys

seed = int(sys.argv[1])
R = random.Random(seed)

FILES = ["user.go", "order.go", "user_test.go", "core.go", "helpers.go", "parse_json.go",
         "user_id.go", "api.go", "store.go", "http_server.go", "x_linux.go", "billing.go",
         "order_test.go", "doc.go", "a.go", "util.go", "user_store.go", "cache.go"]
SCOPE = ["//declscope:shared", "//declscope:private"]
IGN = ["//declscope:ignore", "//declscope:ignore boundary", "//declscope:ignore qualify",
       "//declscope:ignore surplus", "//declscope:ignore unused", "//declscope:ignore boundary,qualify"]
BASES = ["helper", "load", "user", "order", "parse", "store", "trace", "cache", "id", "json",
         "item", "core", "api", "http", "server", "billing", "util", "userID", "orderItem", "storeCache",
         "newUser", "usersByID", "parseJSON", "loading", "stored", "users", "orders", "caching"]


def dir_comment(p=0.3):
    out = []
    if R.random() < p:
        out.append(R.choice(SCOPE))
    if R.random() < p * 0.5:
        out.append(R.choice(IGN))
    if R.random() < 0.1:
        out.insert(0, "// " + R.choice(["Helper does things.", "It is used a lot.", "TODO: tidy."]))
        if R.random() < 0.5:
            out.insert(1, "//")
    R.shuffle(out) if R.random() < 0.2 else None
    return out


class Gen:
    def __init__(self):
        self.n = 0
        self.decls = []  # (kind, name, file, extra)

    def name(self, exported=False):
        self.n += 1
        b = R.choice(BASES)
        n = b + (str(self.n) if R.random() < 0.7 else "")
        if exported:
            n = n[0].upper() + n[1:]
        # avoid duplicates
        while any(d[1] == n for d in self.decls):
            n = n + "x"
        return n


def main():
    g = Gen()
    files = R.sample(FILES, R.randint(2, 5))
    bodies = {f: [] for f in files}
    nonTest = [f for f in files if not f.endswith("_test.go")]
    if not nonTest:
        files.append("main.go")
        bodies["main.go"] = []
        nonTest = ["main.go"]
    for f in files:
        for _ in range(R.randint(1, 4)):
            kind = R.choice(["func", "var", "const", "struct", "iface", "block", "method", "generic", "iota", "trailing"])
            exp = R.random() < 0.3
            dc = dir_comment()
            if kind == "func":
                n = g.name(exp)
                bodies[f].append((dc, "func %s() {}" % n))
                g.decls.append(("func", n, f, None))
            elif kind == "var":
                n = g.name(exp)
                bodies[f].append((dc, "var %s = %d" % (n, R.randint(0, 9))))
                g.decls.append(("var", n, f, None))
            elif kind == "const":
                n = g.name(exp)
                bodies[f].append((dc, "const %s = %d" % (n, R.randint(0, 9))))
                g.decls.append(("const", n, f, None))
            elif kind == "trailing":
                n = g.name(exp)
                bodies[f].append(([], "var %s = 1 %s" % (n, R.choice(SCOPE + IGN))))
                g.decls.append(("var", n, f, None))
            elif kind == "struct":
                n = g.name(exp)
                fields = []
                lines = []
                embed = [d for d in g.decls if d[0] == "struct" and d[1] != n]
                if embed and R.random() < 0.3:
                    e = R.choice(embed)
                    lines.append("\t" + e[1])
                    fields.append(e[1])
                for i in range(R.randint(1, 3)):
                    fe = R.random() < 0.3
                    fn = ("F" if fe else "f") + str(i) + n.lower()[:3]
                    for c in dir_comment(0.2):
                        lines.append("\t" + c)
                    tag = ' `json:"x"`' if R.random() < 0.1 else ""
                    lines.append("\t%s int%s" % (fn, tag))
                    fields.append(fn)
                bodies[f].append((dc, "type %s struct {\n%s\n}" % (n, "\n".join(lines))))
                g.decls.append(("struct", n, f, fields))
            elif kind == "iface":
                n = g.name(exp)
                ms = []
                lines = []
                for i in range(R.randint(1, 2)):
                    mn = ("M" if R.random() < 0.3 else "m") + str(i) + n.lower()[:3]
                    lines.append("\t%s()" % mn)
                    ms.append(mn)
                bodies[f].append((dc, "type %s interface {\n%s\n}" % (n, "\n".join(lines))))
                g.decls.append(("iface", n, f, ms))
            elif kind == "block":
                kw = R.choice(["var", "const"])
                names = [g.name(R.random() < 0.3) for _ in range(R.randint(1, 3))]
                lines = []
                for x in names:
                    for c in dir_comment(0.2):
                        lines.append("\t" + c)
                    lines.append("\t%s = %d" % (x, R.randint(0, 9)))
                    g.decls.append((kw, x, f, None))
                bodies[f].append((dc, "%s (\n%s\n)" % (kw, "\n".join(lines))))
            elif kind == "iota":
                tn = g.name(exp)
                names = [g.name(R.random() < 0.4) for _ in range(R.randint(2, 3))]
                lines = ["\t%s %s = iota" % (names[0], tn)] + ["\t" + x for x in names[1:]]
                bodies[f].append(([], "type %s int" % tn))
                g.decls.append(("type", tn, f, None))
                bodies[f].append((dc, "const (\n%s\n)" % "\n".join(lines)))
                for x in names:
                    g.decls.append(("const", x, f, None))
            elif kind == "generic":
                n = g.name(exp)
                bodies[f].append((dc, "type %s[T any] struct {\n\tv T\n}" % n))
                g.decls.append(("generic", n, f, None))
            elif kind == "method":
                ts = [d for d in g.decls if d[0] in ("struct",)]
                if not ts:
                    continue
                t = R.choice(ts)
                mn = g.name(exp)
                ptr = "*" if R.random() < 0.5 else ""
                bodies[f].append((dc, "func (r %s%s) %s() {}" % (ptr, t[1], mn)))
                g.decls.append(("method", mn, f, t[1]))
    # uses
    for f in files:
        uses = []
        vis = [d for d in g.decls if f.endswith("_test.go") or not d[2].endswith("_test.go")]
        k = 0
        for _ in range(R.randint(0, 6)):
            if not vis:
                break
            d = R.choice(vis)
            kind, n, df, extra = d
            k += 1
            if kind == "func":
                uses.append("\t%s()" % n)
            elif kind in ("var", "const"):
                uses.append("\t_ = %s" % n)
            elif kind == "type":
                uses.append("\tvar _ %s" % n)
            elif kind == "generic":
                uses.append("\t_ = %s[int]{}" % n)
            elif kind == "struct":
                c = R.random()
                if c < 0.25:
                    uses.append("\tvar _ %s" % n)
                elif c < 0.5 and extra:
                    uses.append("\t_ = %s{%s: %s}" % (n, extra[-1], "1" if extra[-1][0] in "fF" else "%s{}" % extra[-1]))
                elif c < 0.7:
                    uses.append("\t_ = new(%s).%s" % (n, R.choice(extra)))
                else:
                    uses.append("\t_ = &%s{}" % n)
            elif kind == "iface":
                uses.append("\tvar iv%d %s\n\tif iv%d != nil { iv%d.%s() }" % (k, n, k, k, R.choice(extra)))
            elif kind == "method":
                uses.append("\t_ = (*%s).%s" % (extra, n))
        if uses:
            fn = "use" + "".join(w.capitalize() for w in f[:-3].replace("-", "_").split("_"))
            bodies[f].append(([], "func %s() {\n%s\n}" % (fn, "\n".join(uses))))
            g.decls.append(("func", fn, f, None))
    out = []
    cfg = []
    if R.random() < 0.6:
        if R.random() < 0.3:
            cfg += ["defaults:", "  unexported: " + R.choice(["shared", "private"])]
        cfg.append("rules:")
        cfg.append("  naming:")
        cfg.append("    qualify: " + R.choice(["always", "ondemand", "never", "ondemand"]))
        cfg.append("    exported: " + R.choice(["true", "false"]))
        if R.random() < 0.3:
            cfg.append("    vocabulary:")
            cfg.append("      user: [usr, account]")
            if R.random() < 0.5:
                cfg.append("      http: [web]")
        if R.random() < 0.15:
            cfg.append("  boundary: off")
        cfg.append("  surplus: " + R.choice(["strict", "loose", "off", "strict"]))
        cfg.append("  unused: " + R.choice(["strict", "loose", "off", "strict"]))
        if R.random() < 0.25:
            cfg.append("files:")
            cfg.append("  - files: [\"%s\"]" % R.choice(["*_test.go", "user*.go", "x_*.go", "**/doc.go", "core.go"]))
            cfg.append("    rules:")
            cfg.append("      %s" % R.choice(["boundary: off", "surplus: off", "unused: off", "naming:\n        qualify: never"]))
        out.append("-- .declscope.yaml --\n" + "\n".join(cfg))
    for f in files:
        lines = []
        if R.random() < 0.15:
            lines.append(R.choice(["//declscope:core", "//declscope:namespace user", "//declscope:shared",
                                   "//declscope:private", "//declscope:ignore", "//declscope:ignore unused",
                                   "//declscope:namespace order", "//declscope:ignore qualify"]))
            lines.append("")
        lines.append("package p")
        lines.append("")
        for dc, decl in bodies[f]:
            lines.extend(dc)
            lines.append(decl)
            lines.append("")
        out.append("-- p/%s --\n%s" % (f, "\n".join(lines)))
    if R.random() < 0.3:
        exported = [d for d in g.decls if d[1][0].isupper() and not d[2].endswith("_test.go") and d[0] in ("func", "var", "const")]
        if exported:
            d = R.choice(exported)
            use = "%s()" % d[1] if d[0] == "func" else "_ = %s" % d[1]
            out.append("-- p/x_test.go --\npackage p_test\n\nimport \"example.com/m/p\"\n\nfunc useX() { p.%s }\n" % use.replace("_ = ", "_ = p.").replace("p.p.", "p.") if False else
                       "-- p/x_test.go --\npackage p_test\n\nimport \"example.com/m/p\"\n\nvar _ = p.%s\n" % d[1])
    print("\n".join(out))
    print("-- @cmd --")
    print("\n".join(["$X ./...", "$X -json ./...", "$X -fix -diff ./...", "$X -fix ./... ; $X ./...",
                     "$X survey -format=json ./...", "$X inspect ./p",
                     "$X baseline -shrink=false ./... ; cat .declscope-baseline.yaml; $X ./..."]))


main()

        if R.random() < 0.15:

        cfg.append("  surplus: " + R.choice(["strict", "loose", "off", "strict"]))

        if R.random() < 0.25:

            cfg.append("    rules:")

    for f in files:

## Configuration

Every setting is optional. The table below lists each setting and its default value. The YAML block shows all available keys; some values are examples.

```yaml
defaults:
  unexported: private     # shared | private

rules:
  naming:
    qualify: never        # always | never | ondemand
    exported: false       # true | false
    vocabulary:
      mouse: [wheel]
  boundary: on           # off | on
  surplus: strict        # off | loose | strict
  unused: strict         # off | loose | strict

filter:
  only: []              # nothing outside these, when set
  omit:
    - "**/mock_*.go"    # and not these

baseline: .declscope-baseline.yaml
```

| Key | Values | Default | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `defaults.unexported` | `shared`, `private` | `private` | Scope of a declaration that carries no directive and inherits none |
| `rules.naming.qualify` | `always`, `never`, `ondemand` | `never` | When a name must carry its namespace. See [the naming rule](#when-it-applies) |
| `rules.naming.exported` | `true`, `false` | `false` | Whether the naming rule also reaches exported declarations. The rename is never offered there |
| `rules.naming.vocabulary` | Namespace to a list of words | None | Extra words that carry a namespace. See [what carries a namespace](#what-carries-a-namespace) |
| `rules.boundary` | `off`, `on` | `on` | Whether the [`boundary`](#boundary) rule reports. See [reach without a boundary](#reach-without-a-boundary) |
| `rules.surplus` | `off`, `loose`, `strict` | `strict` | How much the [`surplus`](#surplus) rule reports. See [strict](#strict) |
| `rules.unused` | `off`, `loose`, `strict` | `strict` | How much the [`unused`](#unused-directives) rule reports. See [off, loose and strict](#off-loose-and-strict) |
| `filter.only` | Path globs | None | When set, no file outside them is read. Empty places no restriction |
| `filter.omit` | Path globs | None | Files taken back out, whether or not `only` let them through |
| `baseline` | A path relative to the config file | The nearest `.declscope-baseline.yaml` | The [baseline](#adopting-on-an-existing-codebase) to consult |

> [!TIP]
> For the recommended checks, put this in `.declscope.yaml`:
>
> ```yaml
> rules:
>   naming:
>     qualify: ondemand
>     exported: true
> ```
>
> `ondemand` checks names once a package has a second namespace. `exported: true` includes exported declarations. `surplus` and `unused` default to `strict`.

- The file is `.declscope.yaml` or `.declscope.yml`. An empty one changes nothing.
- [`-config`](#flags) names one file, and reads no other.
- An **unknown key is an error**, and so is a value a key does not accept. The message names what the section does take, so a typo never leaves a rule at its default in silence.

`defaults` takes only `unexported`, because an exported declaration has no scope to default.

// scope from.
func (m *model) narrowingChangesUnused(d *decl, dir *directive) bool {
	if m.rules.Unused == "off" {
		return false
	}
	all := m.scopeDirectives()
	before := m.unusedOf(dir, nil, all)
	m.narrowed = d
	defer func() { m.narrowed = nil }()
	return m.unusedOf(dir, nil, all) != before
}

'''

s=s.replace('!m.narrowingChangesUnused(d)','!m.narrowingChangesUnused(d, dir)')

results.content:
### Members A **member** is a name written *inside* a type's declaration: a struct's **field**, or an interface's **method name**. It is written inside its type, so its namespace is the type's file's, and the type's directive reaches it. A **method with a receiver** is not a member. It is an ordinary top-level declaration, and its own file gives it its namespace. | | Package-level declaration | Member | Method with a receiver | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Bounding namespace | Its file's | Its **type**'s file's | Its file's | | Contained by | Its `var`, `const` or `type` block | Its **type** | Nothing | | [Naming rule](#the-naming-rule) | Applies | Does not apply | Only when filed away from its type | The naming rule skips members because a member is never read on its own. Every use writes its value first, so `u.name` hands the reader `u` to follow. A method is read the same way, through its receiver. What Go lacks for a member is encapsulation. Every unexported field is visible to the whole package. The `private` scope supplies it.
A type's methods filed in another file Splitting a type's methods across files is ordinary Go. A builder often declares its state in one file and its chainable methods in another. ```go // statement.go (namespace: statement) package database type Statement struct { Table string wheres []string } ``` ```go // query.go (namespace: query) package database func (s *Statement) Where(cond string) *Statement { s.wheres = append(s.wheres, cond) return s } ``` Writing `Where` in `query.go` is not itself a crossing. The field it reaches is one, and the report lands on `statement.go`. ```console $ declscope ./... statement.go:5:2: field Statement.wheres is private to namespace "statement", but is used from namespace "query" query.go:4:4: used here, in namespace "query" query.go:4:22: used here, in namespace "query" ``` The naming rule asks the method to carry `query`. A method is read through its receiver, and `s.Where` points the reader at `Statement`'s unit, which does not hold it. ```console query.go:3:21: method Where does not carry namespace "query" anywhere in its name; rename it to QueryWhere, or to another name that carries "query" ``` Neither report asks for a rename here. The two files are one unit split in two, and `//declscope:namespace statement` on `query.go` settles both.
> [!TIP] > An unexported interface method is the **sealed interface** idiom. Only this package can spell the name, so only this package can implement the interface. declscope gives it file granularity. > > Satisfying an interface is **not** a use of the name, because a method set is resolved, not written. Naming the method does cross. > [!WARNING] > Operations on the **whole value** name no field: copying it, comparing it, zeroing it. They are outside what declscope can see. See [Limits](#limits). ## Rules A **rule** is one check. A rule's name is the diagnostic's category, its [baseline](#adopting-on-an-existing-codebase) key, and what [`//declscope:ignore`](#directives) targets. Declarations the rule never reaches [Members](#members) and [the core namespace](#the-core-namespace) are explained in their own sections. It is an ordinary top-level declaration, and its own file gives it its namespace. | | Package-level declaration | Member | Method with a receiver | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Bounding namespace | Its file's | Its **type**'s file's | Its file's | | Contained by | Its `var`, `const` or `type` block | Its **type** | Nothing | | [Naming rule](#the-naming-rule) | Applies | Does not apply | Only when filed away from its type | The naming rule skips members because a member is never read on its own. Every use writes its value first, so `u.name` hands the reader `u` to follow. A method is read the same way, through its receiver. What Go lacks for a member is encapsulation. Every unexported field is visible to the whole package. The `private` scope supplies it.
A type's methods filed in another file Splitting a type's methods across files is ordinary Go. A builder often declares its state in one file and its chainable methods in another. ```go // statement.go (namespace: statement) package database type Statement struct { Table string wheres []string } ``` ```go // query.go (namespace: query) package database func (s *Statement) Where(cond string) *Statement { s.wheres = append(s.wheres, cond) return s } ``` Writing `Where` in `query.go` is not itself a crossing. The field it reaches is one, and the report lands on `statement.go`. ```console $ declscope ./... statement.go:5:2: field Statement.wheres is private to namespace "statement", but is used from namespace "query" query.go:4:4: used here, in namespace "query" query.go:4:22: used here, in namespace "query" ``` The naming rule asks the method to carry `query`. A method is read through its receiver, and `s.Where` points the reader at `Statement`'s unit, which does not hold it. ```console query.go:3:21: method Where does not carry namespace "query" anywhere in its name; rename it to QueryWhere, or to another name that carries "query" ``` Neither report asks for a rename here. The two files are one unit split in two, and `//declscope:namespace statement` on `query.go` settles both.
> [!TIP] > An unexported interface method is the **sealed interface** idiom. Only this package can spell the name, so only this package can implement the interface. declscope gives it file granularity. > > Satisfying an interface is **not** a use of the name, because a method set is resolved, not written. Naming the method does cross. > [!WARNING] > Operations on the **whole value** name no field: copying it, comparing it, zeroing it. They are outside what declscope can see. See [Limits](#limits). ## Rules A **rule** is one check. A rule's name is the diagnostic's category, its [baseline](#adopting-on-an-existing-codebase) key, and what [`//declscope:ignore`](#directives) targets. Declarations the rule never reaches [Members](#members) and [the core namespace](#the-core-namespace) are explained in their own sections.
DeclarationExampleReason
A member, or a method written beside its type ```go // user.go type user struct{ name string } func (u user) greet() string { return u.name } ```

mkdir -p /tmp/cases_x && cd /tmp/cases_x && rm -f *.txtar && mk() { name=$1; use=$2; cat > $name.txtar <<EOF
-- .declscope.yaml --
defaults:
  unexported: shared
-- p/billing.go --
$(cat)
-- p/http_server.go --
package p

func useHTTP() { $use }
-- @cmd --
\$X -json ./...
EOF
}
mk x1 "_ = orders" <<'EOF'
//declscope:shared

package p

var orders = 1
EOF
mk x2 "" <<'EOF'
//declscope:shared

package p

var orders = 1
EOF
mk x3 "_ = orders" <<'EOF'
package p

//declscope:shared
var orders = 1
EOF
mk x4 "" <<'EOF'
package p

//declscope:shared
var orders = 1
EOF
mk x5 "_ = orders" <<'EOF'
//declscope:shared

package p

//declscope:ignore
var orders = 1
EOF
mk x6 "_ = orders" <<'EOF'
//declscope:shared

package p

//declscope:ignore
var (
	orders = 1
)
EOF
for c in x1 x2 x3 x4 x5 x6; do echo "== $c"; awk '/^-- @cmd --$/{exit} {print}' $c.txtar | /tmp/mk.sh /tmp/xx_$c; cd /tmp/xx_$c; for b in /workspace/executable /tmp/mybin; do $b -json ./... | python3 -c '
import json,sys
d=json.load(sys.stdin)
for pkg,v in d.items():
  for an,diags in v.items():
    for x in diags:
      fx=x.get("suggested_fixes")
      print("  '$( [ $b = /tmp/mybin ] && echo M || echo O)'", x["posn"].split("/")[-1], x["message"], "[FIX: "+fx[0]["message"]+"]" if fx else "")'; done; cd /tmp/cases_x; done
arguments.description: Probe redundant shared directive fixes with cross-namespace uses

	names *directive

#!/bin/bash
# usage: porder_gen.sh dir k t  -> package with k non-test files and t test files, all using helper zz in a.go
dir=$1; k=$2; t=$3
rm -rf $dir; mkdir -p $dir/p
printf 'module example.com/m\n\ngo 1.27\n' > $dir/go.mod
printf 'rules:\n  naming:\n    qualify: always\n' > $dir/.declscope.yaml
names=(a b c d e f g h)
for ((i=0;i<k;i++)); do n=${names[$i]}
  if [ $i -eq 0 ]; then printf 'package p\n\n//declscope:shared\nfunc zz() {}\n\nfunc aUse() { zz() }\n' > $dir/p/$n.go
  else printf 'package p\n\nfunc %sUse() { zz() }\n' $n > $dir/p/$n.go; fi
done
tn=(t u v w)
for ((i=0;i<t;i++)); do n=${tn[$i]}
  printf 'package p\n\nfunc %sTestUse() { zz() }\n' $n > $dir/p/${n}_test.go
done
EOF
chmod +x /tmp/porder_gen.sh
for k in 1 2 3 4 5; do for t in 0 1 2; do d=/tmp/porder/k${k}t${t}; /tmp/porder_gen.sh $d $k $t; cd $d; echo "== k=$k t=$t"; for i in $(seq 1 20); do /workspace/executable -json ./... 2>/dev/null | python3 /tmp/editorder.py; done | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -3; echo "   mine: $(/tmp/mybin_exp -json ./... 2>/dev/null | python3 /tmp/editorder.py)"; done; done

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Random shrink cases around methods, interfaces and conversions: txtar to stdout."""
import random
import sys

seed = int(sys.argv[1])
R = random.Random(seed)

out = ["-- go.mod --\nmodule example.com/app\n\ngo 1.22\n"]
types_ = []
lines = ["package a", ""]
n = [0]


def nm(base):
    n[0] += 1
    return "%s%d" % (base, n[0])


for _ in range(R.randint(1, 3)):
    t = nm("Type")
    ms = [nm("M") for _ in range(R.randint(1, 3))]
    ptr = R.random() < 0.5
    fields = [nm("F") for _ in range(R.randint(0, 2))]
    lines.append("type %s struct {\n%s\n}" % (t, "\n".join("\t%s int" % f for f in fields) or "\tx int"))
    for m in ms:
        lines.append("func (r %s%s) %s() {}" % ("*" if ptr else "", t, m))
    lines.append("func New%s() %s%s { return &%s{} }" % (t, "*" if ptr else "", t, t) if ptr else "func New%s() %s { return %s{} }" % (t, t, t))
    types_.append((t, ms, ptr, fields))
    lines.append("")
# an internal interface
if R.random() < 0.5:
    t = R.choice(types_)
    iname = nm("Iface")
    ims = R.sample(t[1], R.randint(1, len(t[1])))
    lines.append("type %s interface {\n%s\n}" % (iname, "\n".join("\t%s()" % m for m in ims)))
    if R.random() < 0.5:
        lines.append("var _ %s = %sNew%s()" % (iname, "", t[0]))
out.append("-- internal/a/a.go --\n" + "\n".join(lines) + "\n")

# api package
api = ["package api", "", 'import "example.com/app/internal/a"', ""]
uses = []
for t in types_:
    r = R.random()
    if r < 0.25:
        # interface with some methods, conversion
        iname = nm("I")
        ims = R.sample(t[1], R.randint(1, len(t[1])))
        api.append("type %s interface {\n%s\n}" % (iname, "\n".join("\t%s()" % m for m in ims)))
        target = R.choice(["var _ %s = a.New%s()", "func get%s() %s { return a.New%s() }"])
        if target.startswith("var"):
            uses.append(target % (iname, t[0]))
        else:
            fn = nm("Get")
            api.append("func %s() %s { return a.New%s() }" % (fn, iname, t[0]))
    elif r < 0.5:
        uses.append("_ = a.New%s()" % t[0])
    elif r < 0.65:
        uses.append("a.New%s().%s()" % (t[0], R.choice(t[1])))
    elif r < 0.8:
        uses.append("var _ any = a.New%s()" % t[0])
    elif r < 0.9 and t[3]:
        uses.append("_ = a.%s{%s: 1}" % (t[0], R.choice(t[3])))
api.append("func Use() {\n%s\n}" % "\n".join("\t" + u if not u.startswith("var _") or True else u for u in uses))
out.append("-- api/api.go --\n" + "\n".join(api) + "\n")
if R.random() < 0.3:
    t = R.choice(types_)
    out.append("-- internal/a/a_test.go --\npackage a_test\n\nimport \"example.com/app/internal/a\"\n\nfunc useX() {\n\ta.New%s().%s()\n}\n" % (t[0], R.choice(t[1])))
print("\n".join(out))
print("-- @cmd --")
print("$X shrink; echo \"exit $?\"")
print("$X shrink -fix >/dev/null 2>&1; go build ./... && echo BUILD_OK; cat internal/a/a.go")

srcs = sorted(glob.glob("/tmp/cases_s3/*.txtar"))[:60] + sorted(glob.glob("/tmp/cases_g3/*.txtar"))[:60]
for i, path in enumerate(srcs):
    txt = open(path).read()
    files, cmds = txt.split("-- @cmd --")
    lines = files.split("\n")
    for _ in range(R.randint(1, 2)):
        idx = R.randrange(len(lines))
        if lines[idx].startswith("-- ") or idx == 0:
            continue
        op = R.random()
        if op < 0.4:
            del lines[idx]
        elif op < 0.7:
            lines.insert(idx, lines[idx])
        else:
            lines[idx] = lines[idx][: len(lines[idx]) // 2]
    out = "\n".join(lines) + "-- @cmd --\n$X ./...; echo \"exit $?\"\n$X survey ./...; echo \"exit $?\"\n$X baseline ./...; echo \"exit $?\"\n$X shrink; echo \"exit $?\"\n$X shrink -fix; echo \"exit $?\"\n"
    open("/tmp/cases_mut2/mv%d.txtar" % i, "w").write(out)
EOF

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Random multi-package module for survey/inspect/baseline: txtar to stdout."""
import random
import sys
import subprocess

seed = int(sys.argv[1])
R = random.Random(seed)


def pkg_case(pkgdir):
    # reuse gen2 body generation by invoking it and renaming the package dir
    s = subprocess.run(["python3", "/tmp/gen/gen2.py", str(R.randint(1, 10**6))], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
    files = s.split("-- @cmd --")[0]
    out = []
    cfg = None
    for part in files.split("\n-- ")[0:]:
        pass
    blocks = []
    cur = None
    for line in files.split("\n"):
        if line.startswith("-- ") and line.endswith(" --"):
            cur = [line[3:-3], []]
            blocks.append(cur)
        elif cur is not None:
            cur[1].append(line)
    for name, lines in blocks:
        body = "\n".join(lines)
        if name == ".declscope.yaml":
            cfg = body
            continue
        name = name.replace("p/", pkgdir + "/", 1)
        pkgname = pkgdir.split("/")[-1]
        body = body.replace("package p_test", "package %s_test" % pkgname).replace("package p\n", "package %s\n" % pkgname)
        body = body.replace('"example.com/m/p"', '"example.com/m/%s"' % pkgdir).replace("p.", pkgname + ".") if name.endswith("x_test.go") else body
        out.append("-- %s --\n%s" % (name, body))
    return out, cfg


parts = []
dirs = R.sample(["p", "q", "lib/r", "svc/s"], R.randint(2, 3))
for d in dirs:

199:> Without `-a`, `go vet` can report the result of the old configuration. New diagnostics can be missing, and old ones can remain. Running `declscope` directly is not affected.
283:> For the recommended checks, put this in `.declscope.yaml`:
473:> Under `strict`, changing `defaults.unexported` changes the reports. With `unexported: shared`, every `//declscope:shared` on an unexported declaration that nothing else widens is reported, and one `-fix` run deletes them. `loose` never reports a directive only because it names the current default.
718:> Exportedness decides the default, and nothing else. An **exported field of an unexported type** still resolves to `shared`, so making the type unexported protects nothing.
720:> State the boundary instead. `//declscope:private` on the type binds every field it reaches.
791:> An unexported interface method is the **sealed interface** idiom. Only this package can spell the name, so only this package can implement the interface. declscope gives it file granularity.
793:> Satisfying an interface is **not** a use of the name, because a method set is resolved, not written. Naming the method does cross.
796:> Operations on the **whole value** name no field: copying it, comparing it, zeroing it. They are outside what declscope can see. See [Limits](#limits).
850:> This is not how to adopt declscope gradually. A [baseline](#adopting-on-an-existing-codebase) records what a codebase already has and still reports what is new. A switch reports nothing, so you never learn what turning it on later would cost.
869:> The rule is opt-in because whether a prefix reads well depends on the file name, and no tool can see that. A prefix from `comments.go` reads as a noun phrase, `commentsAttached`. A prefix from `collect.go` reads as a command, `collectAddFunc`.
1011:> The vocabulary is for the irregular few. A namespace that needs a long list is a sign that the file declares things it is not about. Splitting the file says more than listing them.
1025:> Sometimes the namespace is what is wrong, not the name. A file name may hold words that name no unit.
1031:> The unit here is `user`, not `userRepository`. `//declscope:namespace user` on the file settles the rule and leaves every name alone.
1038:> Go resolves a name from the inside out, so a new name that is free at package level can still be bound at a use site. The wrong rename **compiles and computes something else**.
1079:> The rule concludes from an **absence**. A directive can hold up something declscope cannot see, so the rule stays quiet on any doubt. For the same reason `loose` offers no fix: its advice is to delete a directive.
1133:> Convention puts private fields last, after the fields other namespaces read. The fix never reorders fields: order is observable through unkeyed composite literals, positional encodings, `unsafe` offsets and 64-bit atomic alignment. Move them yourself where none of those apply.
1464:> Two uses are outside what `shrink` can see. Silence either with the ignore below.
1549:> Look for the row with nothing reported, much baselined and nothing declared. Nothing was decided there, everything was deferred, and the analyzer alone calls it clean.
1712:> A regeneration records what one build configuration sees. A module that runs declscope under several `GOFLAGS=-tags=...` or `GOOS` settings keeps only the last run's entries.
1771:> Some packages cannot reach the working directory by that lookup, such as one in another module. The run then **refuses** and names them, rather than recording entries nothing would find.

718:> Exportedness decides the default, and nothing else. An **exported field of an unexported type** still resolves to `shared`, so making the type unexported protects nothing.
720:> State the boundary instead. `//declscope:private` on the type binds every field it reaches.
791:> An unexported interface method is the **sealed interface** idiom. Only this package can spell the name, so only this package can implement the interface. declscope gives it file granularity.
793:> Satisfying an interface is **not** a use of the name, because a method set is resolved, not written. Naming the method does cross.
796:> Operations on the **whole value** name no field: copying it, comparing it, zeroing it. They are outside what declscope can see. See [Limits](#limits).
850:> This is not how to adopt declscope gradually. A [baseline](#adopting-on-an-existing-codebase) records what a codebase already has and still reports what is new. A switch reports nothing, so you never learn what turning it on later would cost.
869:> The rule is opt-in because whether a prefix reads well depends on the file name, and no tool can see that. A prefix from `comments.go` reads as a noun phrase, `commentsAttached`. A prefix from `collect.go` reads as a command, `collectAddFunc`.
1011:> The vocabulary is for the irregular few. A namespace that needs a long list is a sign that the file declares things it is not about. Splitting the file says more than listing them.
1025:> Sometimes the namespace is what is wrong, not the name. A file name may hold words that name no unit.
1031:> The unit here is `user`, not `userRepository`. `//declscope:namespace user` on the file settles the rule and leaves every name alone.
1038:> Go resolves a name from the inside out, so a new name that is free at package level can still be bound at a use site. The wrong rename **compiles and computes something else**.
1079:> The rule concludes from an **absence**. A directive can hold up something declscope cannot see, so the rule stays quiet on any doubt. For the same reason `loose` offers no fix: its advice is to delete a directive.
1133:> Convention puts private fields last, after the fields other namespaces read. The fix never reorders fields: order is observable through unkeyed composite literals, positional encodings, `unsafe` offsets and 64-bit atomic alignment. Move them yourself where none of those apply.
1464:> Two uses are outside what `shrink` can see. Silence either with the ignore below.
1549:> Look for the row with nothing reported, much baselined and nothing declared. Nothing was decided there, everything was deferred, and the analyzer alone calls it clean.
1712:> A regeneration records what one build configuration sees. A module that runs declscope under several `GOFLAGS=-tags=...` or `GOOS` settings keeps only the last run's entries.
1771:> Some packages cannot reach the working directory by that lookup, such as one in another module. The run then **refuses** and names them, rather than recording entries nothing would find.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Random file-name/decl-name generator stressing the naming rule: txtar to stdout."""
import random
import sys

seed = int(sys.argv[1])
R = random.Random(seed)

WORDS = ["user", "users", "store", "storage", "story", "company", "companies", "http", "url", "id", "ids",
         "json", "api", "order", "billing", "bill", "cache", "caching", "parse", "parser", "load", "loader",
         "item", "entry", "entries", "copy", "make", "making", "made", "run", "running", "address", "status",
         "data", "index", "box", "boxes", "match", "matches", "city", "cities", "key", "keys", "go", "x"]
SUFFIX = ["", "", "", "_test", "_linux", "_amd64", "_windows_arm64", "_js", "_v2", "2"]


def ident(words, exported):
    parts = []
    for i, w in enumerate(words):
        if i == 0 and not exported:
            parts.append(w if R.random() < 0.8 else w.upper() if len(w) <= 4 else w)
        else:
            if w in ("http", "url", "id", "ids", "json", "api") and R.random() < 0.6:
                parts.append(w.upper() if w != "ids" else "IDs")
            else:
                parts.append(w.capitalize())
    s = "".join(parts)
    if exported:
        s = s[0].upper() + s[1:]
    return s


files = []
for _ in range(R.randint(2, 4)):
    words = R.sample(WORDS, R.randint(1, 2))
    sep = R.choice(["_", "_", "-", "."]) if len(words) > 1 else ""
    name = sep.join(words) + R.choice(SUFFIX) + ".go"
    if name not in files and not name.startswith((".", "_")):
        files.append(name)
used = set()
out = []
cfg = ["rules:", "  naming:", "    qualify: %s" % R.choice(["always", "ondemand"]), "    exported: %s" % R.choice(["true", "false"])]
if R.random() < 0.4:
    cfg.append("    vocabulary:")
    for _ in range(R.randint(1, 2)):
        cfg.append("      %s: [%s]" % (R.choice(WORDS), ", ".join(R.sample(WORDS, R.randint(1, 2)))))
out.append("-- .declscope.yaml --\n" + "\n".join(cfg) + "\n")
for f in files:
    lines = []
    if R.random() < 0.1:
        lines += ["//declscope:namespace %s" % R.choice(["user", "store", "billingInfo", "httpServer"]), ""]
    lines += ["package p", ""]
    for _ in range(R.randint(2, 5)):
        n = ident(R.sample(WORDS, R.randint(1, 3)), R.random() < 0.3)
        if n in used or n in ("go",):
            continue
        used.add(n)
        lines.append(R.choice(["func %s() {}", "var %s = 1", "const %s = 2", "type %s int"]) % n)
    out.append("-- p/%s --\n%s\n" % (f, "\n".join(lines)))
print("".join(out))
print("-- @cmd --")
print("$X ./...\n$X -fix ./... ; $X ./...\n$X inspect -format=json ./p")

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Random baseline routing scenarios: txtar to stdout."""
import random
import sys

seed = int(sys.argv[1])
R = random.Random(seed)

pkgs = R.sample(["a", "b", "sub/c", "sub/d", "sub/deep/e"], R.randint(2, 4))
out = ["-- go.mod --\nmodule example.com/m\n\ngo 1.22\n"]
for p in pkgs:
    name = p.split("/")[-1]
    out.append("-- %s/user.go --\npackage %s\n\nfunc helper() {}\n\nvar cache = 1\n" % (p, name))
    out.append("-- %s/order.go --\npackage %s\n\nfunc orderUse() { helper(); _ = cache }\n" % (p, name))
# configs
cfgdirs = R.sample(["", "sub", "a", "sub/deep"], R.randint(0, 2))
for d in cfgdirs:
    lines = []
    if R.random() < 0.6:
        lines.append("baseline: %s" % R.choice(["base.yaml", "../base.yaml", "out/b.yaml", ".declscope-baseline.yaml"]))
    if R.random() < 0.5:
        lines += ["rules:", "  naming:", "    qualify: always"]
    if not lines:
        lines = ["rules:", "  unused: loose"]
    out.append("-- %s.declscope.yaml --\n%s\n" % ((d + "/") if d else "", "\n".join(lines)))
# pre-existing baseline files
for d in R.sample(["", "sub", "a"], R.randint(0, 2)):
    out.append("-- %s.declscope-baseline.yaml --\npackages: {}\n" % ((d + "/") if d else ""))
print("".join(out))
print("-- @cmd --")
cmds = []
for _ in range(4):
    cwd = R.choice([".", ".", "sub", "a"])
    pat = R.choice(["./...", "./...", "."])
    flags = R.choice(["", "", "-merge", "-o out.yaml", "-shrink=false"])
    cmds.append("(cd %s 2>/dev/null && $X baseline %s %s; echo \"exit $?\"); find . -name '*.yaml' | sort | xargs -I{} sh -c 'echo \"== {}\"; cat {}'" % (cwd, flags, pat))
cmds.append("$X baseline ./... ; $X ./...; echo \"exit $?\"")
print("\n".join(cmds))

arguments.command:
mkdir -p /tmp/cases_s6 && cd /tmp/cases_s6 && rm -f *.txtar && for i in $(seq 1 150); do python3 /tmp/gen/gen3.py $((i+5000)) | python3 -c '
import sys, random
R = random.Random('$i')
txt = sys.stdin.read()
files, cmds = txt.split("-- @cmd --")
out = []
for line in files.split("\n"):
    if line.startswith(("func ", "var ", "const ", "type ")) and R.random() < 0.2:
        out.append(R.choice(["//declscope:ignore overexported", "//declscope:ignore", "//declscope:ignore overexported,boundary", "//declscope:ignore boundary"]))
    out.append(line)
    if line.startswith("package ") and R.random() < 0.1:
        pass
res = "\n".join(out)

print(res)
' > s$i.txtar; done; MINE=/tmp/mybin /tmp/dtall.sh /tmp/cases_s6/*.txtar 2>&1 | grep FAIL | head -30; awk '/^RESULT/{p+=$3; f+=$4} END{print "passed", p, "failed", f}' /tmp/dtres/summary.txt

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Shrink rename stress: embedding, promotion, interfaces, conflicts. txtar to stdout."""
import random
import sys

seed = int(sys.argv[1])
R = random.Random(seed)
NAMES = ["Run", "Stop", "Item", "Value", "Name", "ID", "Load", "Save", "Get", "Set", "Close", "Open", "Key", "Data"]

lines = ["package u", ""]
types_ = []
for ti in range(R.randint(2, 4)):
    t = R.choice(["T", "S", "Box", "Item", "Holder", "Node", "Pair"]) + str(ti)
    fields = []
    for _ in range(R.randint(0, 3)):
        f = R.choice(NAMES + [x.lower() for x in NAMES])
        if f not in fields:
            fields.append(f)
    emb = []
    if types_ and R.random() < 0.5:
        e = R.choice(types_)[0]
        emb.append(("*" if R.random() < 0.3 else "") + e)
    body = ["\t" + e for e in emb] + ["\t%s int" % f for f in fields]
    lines.append("type %s struct {\n%s\n}" % (t, "\n".join(body)))
    meths = []
    for _ in range(R.randint(0, 3)):
        m = R.choice(NAMES + [x.lower() for x in NAMES])
        if m in fields or m in meths:
            continue
        meths.append(m)
        lines.append("func (%s%s) %s() {}" % ("*" if R.random() < 0.4 else "", t, m))
    types_.append((t, fields, meths, emb))
    lines.append("")
ifaces = []
for ii in range(R.randint(0, 2)):
    i = R.choice(["runner", "Getter", "closer", "Namer"]) + str(ii)
    ms = R.sample(NAMES + [x.lower() for x in NAMES], R.randint(1, 2))
    lines.append("type %s interface {\n%s\n}" % (i, "\n".join("\t%s()" % m for m in ms)))
    ifaces.append((i, ms))
# internal uses
uses = []
for t, fields, meths, emb in types_:
    if R.random() < 0.5 and meths:
        uses.append("%s{}.%s()" % (t, R.choice(meths)) if "*" not in t else "")
    if R.random() < 0.5 and fields:
        uses.append("_ = %s{}.%s" % (t, R.choice(fields)))
    if emb and R.random() < 0.5:
        uses.append("_ = %s{}.%s" % (t, emb[0].lstrip("*")))
for i, ms in ifaces:
    if R.random() < 0.5:
        uses.append("var _ %s" % i)
lines.append("func use() {\n%s\n}" % "\n".join("\t" + u for u in uses if u))
api = ["package api", "", 'import "example.com/app/internal/u"', ""]
for t, fields, meths, emb in types_:
    if R.random() < 0.5:
        api.append("var _ = u.%s{}" % t)
    if R.random() < 0.2:
        exported = [m for m in meths if m[0].isupper()]
        if exported:
            api.append("func use%s() { new(u.%s).%s() }" % (t, t, R.choice(exported)))
print("-- go.mod --\nmodule example.com/app\n\ngo 1.22\n")
print("-- internal/u/u.go --\n" + "\n".join(lines) + "\n")
print("-- api/api.go --\n" + "\n".join(api) + "\n")
print("-- @cmd --")
print("go build ./... >/dev/null 2>&1 || echo BROKEN_INPUT; $X shrink; echo \"exit $?\"")
print("$X shrink -fix; echo \"exit $?\"; go build ./... && echo BUILD_OK; cat internal/u/u.go")

    lines.append("type %s interface {\n%s\n}" % (i, "\n".join("\t%s()" % m for m in ms)))
    ifaces.append((i, ms))
# internal uses
uses = []
for t, fields, meths, emb in types_:
    if R.random() < 0.5 and meths:
        uses.append("%s{}.%s()" % (t, R.choice(meths)) if "*" not in t else "")
    if R.random() < 0.5 and fields:
        uses.append("_ = %s{}.%s" % (t, R.choice(fields)))
    if emb and R.random() < 0.5:
        uses.append("_ = %s{}.%s" % (t, emb[0].lstrip("*")))
for i, ms in ifaces:
    if R.random() < 0.5:
        uses.append("var _ %s" % i)
lines.append("func use() {\n%s\n}" % "\n".join("\t" + u for u in uses if u))
api = ["package api", "", 'import "example.com/app/internal/u"', ""]
for t, fields, meths, emb in types_:
    if R.random() < 0.5:
        api.append("var _ = u.%s{}" % t)
    if R.random() < 0.2:
        exported = [m for m in meths if m[0].isupper()]
        if exported:
            api.append("func use%s() { new(u.%s).%s() }" % (t, t, R.choice(exported)))
print("-- go.mod --\nmodule example.com/app\n\ngo 1.22\n")
print("-- internal/u/u.go --\n" + "\n".join(lines) + "\n")
print("-- api/api.go --\n" + "\n".join(api) + "\n")
print("-- @cmd --")
print("go build ./... >/dev/null 2>&1 || echo BROKEN_INPUT; $X shrink; echo \"exit $?\"")
print("$X shrink -fix; echo \"exit $?\"; go build ./... && echo BUILD_OK; cat internal/u/u.go")

steps.message:
The Go reimplementation of `declscope` is finished and committed. On a fresh checkout, `./compile.sh` builds it to `./executable`, and it matches the original on every comparison I ran, with two exceptions that can't be closed:

- **`-v` / `-debug=v`**: these print microsecond timestamps, and `-debug=t` prints measured run times. The lines match apart from the clock values.
- **`-json` edits for renames that span several files**: the original lists these edits in a different order from run to run. Every `-json` mismatch I saw disappears once the edits are sorted. I set my order to match what the original produces most often.

**Testing.** Every check compared my build against the original binary on stdout, stderr, exit code and the files left on disk. That covered about 25,000 commands: hand-written cases, the README's Go examples (all 50 extractable groups pass), and random generators for directives, naming, interfaces, multi-package modules, `shrink` renames, baseline routing, and deliberately broken inputs. Nothing crashed.

**Changes this session (34 commits):**
- **Driver flags**: `-v` now works as an alias for `-debug=v`, `-debug=t` prints per-package timings, and `-cpuprofile`, `-memprofile` and `-trace` write real profiles.
- **`shrink`**:
  - It now checks the build lists of the main and nested modules, including vendored copies and lists that can't be read.
  - Several "no fix" reasons were added, among them generated files, names that are predeclared or contain underscores, and names already taken on a type or an embedding type.
  - Constants grouped in one const block are handled correctly when only tests, an ignore or the baseline keep one of them.
  - Renaming a type now also renames the struct fields that embed it.
  - `baseline` no longer reads the old baseline file while regenerating it.
- **Unused-directive rule**: the message wording now depends on outer and inner directives the way the original's does, and the decision to offer or hold back a `-fix` follows its rules (including `//` separator lines and Windows line endings).
- **Surplus rule**: it judges against the configured default, treats methods that an exported type or a matching interface could reach as possibly used, and only offers a fix when the directive would still do something afterwards.
- **Smaller fixes**: where config files are looked for, `-config` paths shown as typed, the "all core" notes in `inspect` and `survey`, creating the folder for a baseline file, and the position of the "package read as empty" report.

One deliberate quirk: in one generated case, `shrink -fix` from the original leaves code that no longer compiles. My version reproduces that rather than fixing it.

The original `./executable` was never overwritten during testing; `compile.sh` will replace it when it runs. The only non-Go code in the repo is the short `compile.sh`.
